\begin{frame}{The problem: every session starts over}
\subt{A six-month research project cannot be reduced to one long chat.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{Reconstruction cost.} Re-explain the question, dataset, code locations, methodological choices and pending work.
\item \textbf{Memory failures.} Earlier caveats or rejected ideas disappear from the model’s accessible context.
\item \textbf{Context rot.} Long conversations can bury important facts among irrelevant traces and repeated instructions.
\item \textbf{Coordination cost.} Coauthors and new agents must infer what the team decided and why.
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Without a Brain}{Chat history + folders + implicit human memory.}
\sboxblue{With a Brain}{Stable restart point, selective retrieval and explicit decision history.}
\end{columns}
\medskip    
\tagline{A durable project needs a state representation, not only a transcript.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{What should the Brain remember?}
\subt{Persist the knowledge required to make the next session productive.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.485\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Project state}{Question, progress, current bottleneck, data and code status.}
\column{.485\textwidth}
\coursebox{Decisions}{Accepted methodological rules, rejected alternatives and rationale.}
\end{columns}\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.485\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Evidence}{Sources, original data pointers, confidence, provenance and uncertainty.}
\column{.485\textwidth}
\coursebox{Procedures}{Commands, validation routines, reusable prompts and skills.}
\end{columns}\vspace{1mm}
\medskip
\tagline{Do not promote every chat message: forget noise, retain durable work.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Own your knowledge, not your model}
\subt{One external vault can be read by different agents when access and instructions are configured.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]
\column{.51\textwidth}\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.5em}\small
\item \textbf{Open representation.} Markdown + optional YAML/JSON metadata, readable in any editor.
\item \textbf{Portability.} Use the same project state from Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or a future agent.
\item \textbf{One source of truth.} Avoid divergent copies of facts in proprietary AI profiles or prompts.
\item \textbf{Qualification.} Skills, permissions, connectors and model behavior are not automatically portable.
\end{itemize}
\column{.46\textwidth}
\begin{chgfig}
\scalebox{0.78}{\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm]

\end{columns}
\medskip
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{New session, same project knowledge}
\subt{Reset the conversation when useful; do not reset the project.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{Before closeout.} Update the current state, next actions, decisions and validated technical notes.
\item \textbf{At startup.} Read global routing instructions; identify the project; load only relevant core files.
\item \textbf{In the new session.} Recover the task constraints without importing the entire previous chat.
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{\chg{Short sessions avoid context rot}}{\chg{Because the state is saved, you can close a session and open a new one often. Each session stays short, so old material never piles up and drowns the facts that matter.}}
\sboxblue{\chg{Load only what the task needs}}{\chg{The new session reads a small index first, then opens only the one or two project files the task requires.}}
\end{columns}
\medskip
\tagline{A good closeout is what makes a clean start possible.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Less context can mean fewer tokens}
\subt{\chg{A worked example: answering a referee on a staggered difference-in-differences paper. Token counts are rough orders of magnitude.}}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.55em}
\item \chg{\textbf{The task.} Referee 2 asks for a pre-trend test. You ask the agent to draft the new event-study paragraph and the reply.}
\item \chg{\textbf{Everything in the prompt.} Full draft (25,000 tokens) + ten related papers (60,000) + do-files and logs (15,000): about \textbf{100,000 tokens}, sent again at every request.}
\item \chg{\textbf{From the Brain.} CURRENT\_STATE and DECISIONS (2,000) + the referee comment and Section 4 (4,000) + the event-study log (2,000): about \textbf{8,000 tokens}, roughly 92\% fewer.}
\end{itemize}
\tagline{Optimize relevant information delivered per token, not token count alone.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Portable skills: instructions on demand}
\subt{A file-based skill transfers a tested workflow from one session or agent to another.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{Catalog.} Name and description tell an agent that a skill exists.
\item \textbf{Activation.} The full SKILL.md procedure loads when the task calls for it.
\item \textbf{Resources.} Scripts, examples and references load only when needed.
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Your implementation}{Cross-project skills in general/capabilities/skills; agent adapters in .agents/skills.}
\sboxblue{\chg{What it costs}}{\chg{At every start the agent reads the list of skill names and one-line descriptions, a few hundred tokens. The full steps of a skill enter the context only when the agent opens it.}}
\end{columns}
\medskip
\tagline{Store once, discover cheaply, load selectively.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{From chatbot to research assistant}
\subt{A paper is a chain of decisions and dependencies, not a sequence of chat messages.}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.565\textwidth}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.48em}\small
\item \textbf{Research question.} What is the mechanism, population and contribution?
\item \textbf{Data design.} How were sources collected, matched, cleaned and validated?
\item \textbf{Identification.} Which assumptions, timing choices and robustness checks are binding?
\item \textbf{Research continuity.} How does the next agent recover a reproducible restart point?
\end{itemize}
\column{.405\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Economics insight}{Memory can lower re-entry and coordination costs for distributed research teams.}
\sboxblue{Research integrity}{An agent should cite evidence and preserve unresolved uncertainty.}
\end{columns}
\medskip
\tagline{The value is a cumulative and auditable work, thus a better answer.}
\end{frame}
